title: Security section says all media is DTLS-encrypted, but the same page describes a non-WebRTC relay path
test: tests/howToSecurityCopy.test.js: 'the blanket "media is encrypted ... WebRTC DTLS" sentence is gone', 'WebRTC viewing, OBS WHIP ingest and WHEP are described as DTLS-SRTP', 'relay media is described as travelling over the page connection, encrypted only as far as that is', 'public links are HTTPS that ends at the tunnel provider', 'a plain-HTTP local link is unencrypted unless local HTTPS is enabled', plus 'the rest of the section is unchanged' (passed before and after)
proof: The test reads src/HowToView.jsx, turns the Security and privacy section into plain text and checks each claim sentence by sentence. On the unchanged page 5 of its 6 tests failed: the old sentence 'Public links use HTTPS, and media is encrypted in transit with WebRTC DTLS' was present, no sentence named DTLS-SRTP, none tied the relay to the page connection, the only public-link sentence did not mention the tunnel provider, and none described the local link. The sixth test (the other sentences of the section stay as they were) passed before and after. The paragraph is now a short list: WebRTC viewing, OBS WHIP ingest and WHEP playback use DTLS-SRTP (WHIP and WHEP create a mediasoup WebRtcTransport in lib/whipRoutes.js and lib/whepRoutes.js, and DTLS fingerprints are required: a WHIP offer without one gets 400); relay media is Socket.IO bytes on the page connection (lib/socket.js media-chunk), so it is encrypted only as far as that connection is (server.js itself warns that 'WebRTC DTLS does not protect relay bytes' for the trusted-LAN relay); public links are HTTPS that ends at the tunnel provider (cloudflared forwards to 127.0.0.1, lib/tunnel.js); a local link is plain HTTP unless LOCAL_HTTPS=true, which lib/https.js serves with a self-signed certificate (section-aa6945a2a9cfd7a199000015/Q-006: HTTP by default, HTTPS opt-in). The rest of the section is unchanged. Not checked in a browser; the copy was checked against the transport code and by `vite build` (built into a scratchpad folder, exit 0).
